title: Payload-only eligibility guards belong in the job-level `if:` of community-label.yml
answers: community-label workflow runs for bot or internal PRs
skip labeling for members, collaborators, and bots before runner starts
why does the community label job still allocate a runner for ineligible PRs
where to add a new exclusion for the community labeling action
body:
Invariant: in `.github/workflows/community-label.yml`, `jobs.label-community.if` holds the cheap event-payload checks: repo is `mlflow/mlflow`, `github.event.pull_request.user.type` is not `Bot`, and `author_association` is not in MEMBER/COLLABORATOR/OWNER.
Why: a job whose `if:` is false never gets a runner, so ineligible PRs cost nothing. A shell `exit 0` runs only after runner allocation.
Do not move these checks back into the `run:` script, and do not re-add `AUTHOR_TYPE`/`ASSOCIATION` env vars just to repeat them there.
The script keeps only checks that need API calls: the `gh api users/$AUTHOR` profile and commit-email Databricks affiliation checks, then labeling.
Any new exclusion that uses only the event payload should go in the `if:` expression, written as a `>-` folded scalar with `&&` joins.
Applies to: changes to community-label.yml or similar labeling workflows in this repo.
applies: Scope: the community-label workflow's job gating; the rule covers payload-only checks, not API-dependent ones.
says: The community contributor label is mistakenly applied to internal team pull requests
Pull requests created by automated bots trigger the community contributor labeling workflow
Wasted automation runner minutes executing community labeling jobs for project team members
Prevent community labeling actions from allocating runners on ineligible internal pull requests
search: In .github/workflows/community-label.yml, event payload eligibility checks must be declared in jobs.label-community.if rather than inside the run script. The job-level if condition verifies the repo is mlflow/mlflow, the pull request author is not a Bot, and author_association excludes MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, and OWNER, preventing runner allocation costs for ineligible PRs. Only API-dependent checks like gh api user profile lookups and commit-email Databricks affiliation remain in the script, while any new payload exclusions must be added to the job if using folded scalars with && joins.
